Claude's conclusion:
### Root cause

`TestDNSFunctionality`'s `Eventually` predicate requires all four ports to have expected DNS servers, eth3 to show a DNS error, and the DPC to be healthy — but **eth1 never acquired an IP address at all** for the entire 420s window (and still hasn't, live). Nim's DPC reconciler log shows it started `dhcpcd` on eth1 at `04:27:48`, the command failed with `exit status 1` ~17s later at `04:28:05` (no lease obtained), and the reconciler then marked the DHCP-client-create as "finalized" without retrying — leaving no `dhcpcd` process at all for eth1 (confirmed live: only eth0/eth2/eth3 have `dhcpcd` processes running). Consequently `DeviceNetworkStatus`/`DevicePortConfig` for eth1 has stuck on `LastError: "interface eth1: no suitable IP address available"` since boot, which permanently fails the "all four ports have expected DNS servers"/"DPC healthy" conditions (eth3's DNS-resolution error, by contrast, is present and expected). SDN-side config for network1/bridge1 (DHCP server, bridge, veth) looks correctly set up, so this looks like a lease that was never obtained/retried on the EVE/nim side rather than an SDN misconfiguration.

This is the same test as a prior ledger entry (2026-11-25, run #54, and recurring since at least 2026-11-22) that also failed on `TestDNSFunctionality` with a stuck `Eventually` loop due to a bad port error, but the earlier entries' root causes were different: a stale "no DNS server available" race on eth2 (2026-11-24/25) and a DPC-reconciler delay applying a DHCP→static change on eth1 (migration test). Today's failure — eth1 never getting a DHCP lease at all, with `dhcpcd` exiting and never being retried — hasn't appeared in the ledger before, so while `TestDNSFunctionality` has a recurring history of DPC/DNS-convergence races, this specific no-IP-on-eth1 failure mode looks new. The broker host is moderately loaded (89% of RAM committed to VMs, load 6.3/40 CPUs, some swap in use) but not clearly overloaded, so it's a plausible but unconfirmed contributing factor to the DHCP timeout rather than a clear cause.

### Root cause

`TestDNSFunctionality` is stuck in its Phase-1 `Eventually` loop because **eth2** keeps reporting `interface eth2: no DNS server available` even though its `DNSServers` field is consistently populated. Live evidence confirms this: `/run/nim/DeviceNetworkStatus/global.json` on the still-paused device shows eth2 with two valid DNS servers (`10.35.7.25`, `10.35.3.25`), and the device-info snapshot's `networkErr` for eth2 carries the "no DNS server available" error at the same timestamp eth0/eth1 report success — a stale/raced error alongside correct current state. The nim logs show this firing on every ~60s DPC-verify cycle (`04:22:30`, `04:23:30`, `04:24:30`, ... `04:27:30`, 40 occurrences total), the same per-cycle pattern as before. The test only tolerates an error on eth3 (deliberately broken), so eth2's spurious error keeps failing the predicate for the full 420s budget.

This is a known, recurring issue: it matches the exact same root cause already documented in the ledger's 2026-11-22 entry (run #39) — eth2 failing `TestConnectivity`/`DNSNotAvailError` despite `DeviceNetworkStatus` showing valid DNS servers for eth2 in the same verify cycle — pointing to a timing race in EVE's DNS-verification path (`dpcmanager`/`netmonitor` sampling a stale resolv.conf view just before the connectivity probe runs). It last appeared on 2026-11-22 and does not appear in the 2026-11-23 or 2026-11-24 ledger entries, so it's intermittent/recurring rather than a brand-new regression from tonight's commits. This is unrelated to tonight's other failure in the same run (`TestLocalNIWithMultiplePorts`'s PortProber slow-convergence timing).

Claude's conclusion:
### Root cause

Phase 1 of `TestDNSFunctionality` never satisfies its predicate because **ethernet2** repeatedly reports a connectivity error of `interface eth2: no DNS server available`, even though its own `DevicePort.dns.DNSservers` consistently lists both valid DNS servers (`10.35.7.25` static + `10.35.3.25` DHCP) — the test only expects eth3 (the deliberately-broken port) to have an error, so the `Eventually` loop keeps timing out over the full 420s/5-plus-minute budget.

Live log evidence from `/run/nim/DeviceNetworkStatus/global.json` and the nim debug log shows this is **not transient**: at 05:11:52, 05:12:52, 05:13:52 and 05:14:52 (once per DPC-verify cycle), nim's `TestConnectivity`/`SendOnIntf` fails eth2 with `types.DNSNotAvailError` (raised by `controllerconn.prepareHTTPClientConfig` when `types.GetDNSServers()` returns zero entries for eth2), yet the `DeviceNetworkStatus` published milliseconds later in that *same* verify cycle already shows eth2's `DNSServers` populated with both entries. This points to a real timing race in EVE's own DNS-verification path — `dpcmanager.updateDNS()`/`netmonitor.GetInterfaceDNSInfo()` samples a stale/empty per-interface resolv.conf view (the boot-time log even shows `"No resolv.conf for eth2"` entries) right before the connectivity probe runs, so the probe for eth2 fails every single retest cycle even though the DNS data it needs is correct and available. eth0/eth1/eth3 never exhibit this: eth0 and eth1 reach `LastSucceeded` normally, and eth3's error is the expected one (bad DNS server, different-network skip).

This does not match any failure in the current run's earlier history (TestDNSFunctionality is the first test in this suite run), and it does not appear in `live-ledger.md`, which only covers 2026-11-20 and 2026-11-21 and has no prior mention of `TestDNSFunctionality` or this DNS-availability race — so this looks like a newly-observed, reproducible EVE-side bug rather than a known/recurring flake or a test-harness defect.
